- changelog.d/4207-release-tag-push-retry.md
  Line or code reference: lines 8-9
  Problem: The "numbers that matter" table states "Maximum publication attempts per tag | 3" and "Retry delays | 2 seconds, then 4 seconds". The implementation in both `.github/workflows/mark-stable.yml:690` and `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:5385` sets `local max_attempts=5` with exponential backoff producing four sleeps of 2s, 4s, 8s, and 16s. The test at `tests/test_mark_stable_release_tag_refspec_contract.py:207` asserts `local max_attempts=5` and the `test_workflow_tag_publication_helper_executes_failure_matrix` test exercises 5 attempts with sleeps 2/4/8/16.
  Why it fails at runtime: Release operators reading the changelog will be misinformed about retry capacity and backoff behavior — they will expect 3 attempts with 2s/4s delays when the actual behavior is 5 attempts with 2s/4s/8s/16s delays. This is the exact defect Copilot flagged in entry[6] of the PR comments and the last autofix run did not address.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
- changelog.d/4211-release-tag-push-retry.md
  Line or code reference: line 4
  Problem: The fragment states "Both ... workflows now wrap the version-tag, `stable` and major-version pushes in a bounded `retry_push` helper." The `retry_push` helper no longer exists in either workflow — the forward-merge from `stable` replaced it with `publish_tag_with_remote_verification`. A grep for `retry_push` across `.github/workflows/*.yml` returns zero matches. The contract test now pins `publish_tag_with_remote_verification`, not `retry_push`.
  Why it fails at runtime: Operators or automated tooling consuming changelogs will be directed to a helper that does not exist. The "For contributors" section at line 17 also says the test "pins the helper" — that helper is now `publish_tag_with_remote_verification`, not `retry_push`.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=5

- changelog.d/4207-release-tag-push-retry.md
  Line or code reference: the "The numbers that matter" table — rows "Maximum publication attempts per tag" and "Retry delays" (the fragment sits inside the diff at lines 1-12; the wrong rows are the third and fourth body lines of that table)
  Problem: The fragment reports "Maximum publication attempts per tag | 3" and "Retry delays | 2 seconds, then 4 seconds". The actual implementation in .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml:684 and .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:5379 sets local max_attempts=5, and the helper's exponential backoff sleeps at 2s, 4s, 8s, and 16s between successive attempts (four sleeps for five attempts). tests/test_mark_stable_release_tag_refspec_contract.py:207 already pins local max_attempts=5 against the helper text, and the unreadable_remote_calls assertion in test_workflow_tag_publication_helper_executes_failure_matrix pins the exact ["sleep:2","sleep:4","sleep:8","sleep:16"] sequence — confirming the implementation is correct and the fragment is factually wrong.
  Why it fails at runtime: Release operators reading the changelog will be misled about retry capacity (3 vs 5) and backoff behavior (2s+4s=6s total vs 2s+4s+8s+16s=30s total). The misleading numbers may also be inherited by automation that parses changelog fragments. Copilot review comment entry[6] (id 4062858094, 2026-09-21T14:02:36Z) flagged this exact defect during this review cycle, and the autofix run that produced the last commit (entry[5] editor summary, 13:49:20Z) did not address it. The fragment is in PR CHANGED FILES, was carried into the PR by the original commit, and remained unfixed across the last autofix.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
